question: How often should tomato crops be irrigated?
answer: Tomato is best irrigated lightly and frequently, especially via drip irrigation, avoiding both waterlogging and drought stress, particularly during flowering and fruit set.

question: What is the ideal soil pH for most crops?
answer: Most crops perform best in a soil pH range of about 6.0 to 7.5 (slightly acidic to neutral); get a soil test done for your specific field before amending pH.

question: When should groundnut be sown?
answer: Groundnut is typically sown at the start of the Kharif season (June-July) or Rabi season (post-monsoon), depending on regional rainfall patterns.

question: How can I identify nitrogen deficiency in a crop?
answer: Nitrogen deficiency commonly shows as uniform yellowing (chlorosis) starting from older, lower leaves, along with stunted and slow overall growth.

question: What causes yellowing of rice leaves?
answer: Yellowing of rice leaves can result from nitrogen deficiency, zinc deficiency, bacterial leaf blight, or waterlogging/drainage stress; the growth stage and pattern of yellowing help narrow the cause.

question: How do I control whitefly organically?
answer: Yellow sticky traps, neem-based sprays, avoiding excess nitrogen, and encouraging natural predators such as ladybird beetles are common organic approaches to manage whitefly.

question: What is crop rotation and why is it important?
answer: Crop rotation is growing different crop types in sequence on the same land across seasons; it helps break pest/disease cycles, balances soil nutrient use, and improves long-term soil health.

question: How does weather affect fertilizer application?
answer: Avoid applying fertilizer immediately before heavy rain since it can wash away nutrients; dry, low-wind conditions are generally best for foliar sprays.

question: When is the best time to harvest rice?
answer: Rice is generally ready for harvest when about 80-85% of the grains have turned golden yellow and the moisture content of the grain has dropped appropriately.

question: What is Integrated Pest Management (IPM)?
answer: IPM combines biological, cultural, mechanical and (as a last resort) chemical methods to manage pests sustainably while minimizing environmental and health risks.

question: Tell me about growing Rice.
answer: Rice (நெல்) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 90-150 days. Staple cereal grown widely in Tamil Nadu deltas; needs standing water for most growth stages. It prefers clayey loam, water-retentive soil and a temperature range of 20-35°C.

question: Tell me about growing Wheat.
answer: Wheat (கோதுமை) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Rabi season, maturing in about 110-130 days. Major cereal in North India; sensitive to waterlogging and needs a cool growing period. It prefers well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 10-25°C.

question: Tell me about growing Maize.
answer: Maize (சோளம்) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 90-110 days. Versatile cereal used for food, fodder and industry; moderate water requirement. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 18-27°C.

question: Tell me about growing Cotton.
answer: Cotton (பருத்தி) is a fibre crop typically grown in the Kharif season, maturing in about 150-180 days. Fibre crop needing a long frost-free season and moderate, well-spaced irrigation. It prefers black cotton soil (regur) soil and a temperature range of 21-30°C.

question: Tell me about growing Sugarcane.
answer: Sugarcane (கரும்பு) is a cash crop crop typically grown in the Year-round (12 month crop) season, maturing in about 300-365 days. Long-duration cash crop with high water demand, propagated via stem cuttings. It prefers deep, well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 21-27°C.

question: Tell me about growing Groundnut.
answer: Groundnut (நிலக்கடலை) is a oilseed/legume crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 100-130 days. Legume oilseed that fixes atmospheric nitrogen and needs calcium during pegging. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-30°C.

question: Tell me about growing Tomato.
answer: Tomato (தக்காளி) is a vegetable crop typically grown in the Year-round (season dependent) season, maturing in about 60-90 days. Widely grown vegetable, sensitive to blossom-end rot and several fungal/bacterial diseases. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-27°C.

question: Tell me about growing Banana.
answer: Banana (வாழை) is a fruit crop typically grown in the Year-round season, maturing in about 10-13 months. High water and nutrient demanding fruit crop, propagated using suckers/tissue-culture plants. It prefers deep, rich, well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 15-35°C.

question: Tell me about growing Chilli.
answer: Chilli (மிளகாய்) is a vegetable/spice crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 120-180 days. Spice crop sensitive to thrips, mites and viral leaf curl disease. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-30°C.

question: Tell me about growing Blackgram.
answer: Blackgram (உளுந்து) is a pulse/legume crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 70-90 days. Short-duration pulse commonly grown as a rice-fallow crop; improves soil nitrogen. It prefers well-drained loam to clay loam soil and a temperature range of 25-35°C.

question: What are the symptoms of Bacterial Leaf Blight?
answer: Bacterial Leaf Blight (பாக்டீரியா இலை கருகல் நோய்) affects Rice and is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae. Symptoms include: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins turning yellow-white and drying from tip inward.

question: How do I manage Bacterial Leaf Blight in Rice?
answer: Management of Bacterial Leaf Blight: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, ensure field sanitation and balanced water management; consult an expert for approved bactericides.

question: What are the symptoms of Rice Blast?
answer: Rice Blast (நெல் வெடிப்பு நோய்) affects Rice and is caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (fungus). Symptoms include: Diamond/spindle shaped grey-centered lesions with brown margins on leaves, neck rot at panicle base.

question: How do I manage Rice Blast in Rice?
answer: Management of Rice Blast: Use resistant varieties, avoid dense nursery, balanced nitrogen; fungicidal seed treatment as advised by an agricultural officer.

question: What are the symptoms of Late Blight?
answer: Late Blight (பிற்பாதி கருகல் நோய்) affects Tomato and is caused by Phytophthora infestans (oomycete). Symptoms include: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems with white fungal growth under humid conditions, fruit rot.

question: How do I manage Late Blight in Tomato?
answer: Management of Late Blight: Improve field drainage and air circulation, remove infected debris, use certified disease-free seedlings; fungicide only under expert guidance.

question: What are the symptoms of Fusarium Wilt?
answer: Fusarium Wilt (பியூசேரியம் வாட்டநோய்) affects Cotton, Tomato, Banana and is caused by Fusarium oxysporum (fungus). Symptoms include: Yellowing and wilting of lower leaves progressing upward, vascular browning inside stem.

question: How do I manage Fusarium Wilt in Cotton?
answer: Management of Fusarium Wilt: Practice crop rotation, use resistant/tolerant varieties, avoid waterlogging, solarize nursery soil before sowing.

question: What are the symptoms of Powdery Mildew?
answer: Powdery Mildew (பொடி பூஞ்சை நோய்) affects Groundnut, Chilli, many crops and is caused by Erysiphe / Oidium spp. (fungus). Symptoms include: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surface, leaf curling and premature drying.

question: How do I manage Powdery Mildew in Groundnut?
answer: Management of Powdery Mildew: Ensure good airflow between plants, avoid excess nitrogen, remove heavily infected leaves; sulfur-based fungicide only per label/expert advice.

question: What are the symptoms of Panama Wilt?
answer: Panama Wilt (பனாமா வாட்டநோய்) affects Banana and is caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense. Symptoms include: Yellowing of older leaves, splitting of pseudostem base, plant collapse.

question: How do I manage Panama Wilt in Banana?
answer: Management of Panama Wilt: Use tissue-culture disease-free planting material, avoid waterlogged soil, do not replant bananas in infected fields for several years.

question: What are the symptoms of Leaf Curl Virus?
answer: Leaf Curl Virus (இலை சுருள் வைரஸ் நோய்) affects Chilli, Tomato and is caused by Begomovirus (whitefly transmitted). Symptoms include: Upward/downward curling of leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruiting.

question: How do I manage Leaf Curl Virus in Chilli?
answer: Management of Leaf Curl Virus: Control whitefly vector with sticky traps and recommended practices, remove infected plants early, use virus-tolerant varieties.

question: What are the symptoms of Blackgram Yellow Mosaic?
answer: Blackgram Yellow Mosaic (மஞ்சள் தேமல் நோய்) affects Blackgram, Greengram and is caused by Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (whitefly transmitted). Symptoms include: Irregular yellow mosaic patches on leaves, stunted pods.

question: How do I manage Blackgram Yellow Mosaic in Blackgram?
answer: Management of Blackgram Yellow Mosaic: Sow tolerant varieties, manage whitefly populations, remove volunteer/alternate host plants near field borders.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Rice?
answer: Urea (யூரியா) supplies Nitrogen (N) - 46% and is suitable for Rice, Maize, Wheat, most cereals. Recommended application: Vegetative growth stage, split doses. Fast-acting nitrogen source promoting leafy growth; apply in split doses to reduce leaching loss.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Most crops at sowing/transplanting?
answer: DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate) (டிஏபி உரம்) supplies Nitrogen (18%) + Phosphorus (46%) and is suitable for Most crops at sowing/transplanting. Recommended application: Basal application at sowing/transplanting. Provides early-stage phosphorus for root development, usually applied as a basal dose.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Fruiting/tuber crops?
answer: MOP (Muriate of Potash) (மியூரியேட் ஆஃப் பொட்டாஷ்) supplies Potassium (K) - 60% and is suitable for Fruiting/tuber crops, sugarcane, banana. Recommended application: Flowering / fruit development stage. Improves fruit quality, disease resistance and drought tolerance; important during reproductive stages.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for All crops?
answer: Farmyard Manure (FYM) (தொழு உரம்) supplies Organic matter, N-P-K + micronutrients and is suitable for All crops. Recommended application: Basal application before sowing/planting. Improves soil structure, water-holding capacity and microbial activity over the long term.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for All crops?
answer: Vermicompost (மண்புழு உரம்) supplies Organic matter, balanced N-P-K + micronutrients and is suitable for All crops, especially vegetables. Recommended application: Basal + top dressing. Slow-release organic fertilizer that improves soil health; widely used in organic farming.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Oilseeds?
answer: Single Super Phosphate (SSP) (சிங்கிள் சூப்பர் பாஸ்பேட்) supplies Phosphorus (16%) + Calcium + Sulphur and is suitable for Oilseeds, pulses, general crops. Recommended application: Basal application at sowing. Economical phosphorus source that also supplies sulphur, useful for oilseed and pulse crops.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Rice?
answer: Zinc Sulphate (துத்தநாக சல்பேட்) supplies Micronutrient - Zinc and is suitable for Rice, Citrus, most crops on zinc-deficient soil. Recommended application: Soil application or foliar spray. Corrects zinc deficiency symptoms such as leaf bronzing/khaira disease in rice; test soil before applying.

question: What fertilizer is suitable for Vegetables?
answer: NPK Complex (19:19:19) (என்பிகே கூட்டு உரம்) supplies Balanced Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium and is suitable for Vegetables, fruit crops, general use. Recommended application: Vegetative and flowering stage, foliar or soil. Water-soluble balanced fertilizer suited for fertigation and foliar feeding programs.

question: How often should Rice crops be irrigated?
answer: For Rice, the recommended method is Flood/Continuous submergence or AWD (Alternate Wetting & Drying). 2-5 cm standing water during vegetative stage; AWD saves water without yield loss Maintaining shallow standing water during flowering is critical; avoid stress at panicle initiation.

question: How often should Wheat crops be irrigated?
answer: For Wheat, the recommended method is Furrow / Sprinkler. 4-6 irrigations at critical growth stages (CRI, tillering, flowering, grain filling) Crown root initiation (CRI) stage irrigation is the most critical for yield.

question: How often should Cotton crops be irrigated?
answer: For Cotton, the recommended method is Drip / Furrow. Irrigate at 50-60% depletion of available soil moisture Avoid water stress during flowering and boll development; drip irrigation improves water-use efficiency.

question: How often should Sugarcane crops be irrigated?
answer: For Sugarcane, the recommended method is Furrow / Drip. Frequent irrigation every 7-10 days depending on soil and season High water requirement crop; drip irrigation with fertigation significantly improves efficiency.

question: How often should Tomato crops be irrigated?
answer: For Tomato, the recommended method is Drip irrigation recommended. Light, frequent irrigation; avoid water stress during flowering/fruit set Irregular watering increases blossom-end rot and fruit cracking.

question: How often should Groundnut crops be irrigated?
answer: For Groundnut, the recommended method is Sprinkler / Furrow. Critical stages: pegging and pod development Avoid waterlogging; groundnut is sensitive to excess soil moisture at sowing.

question: How do I control Brown Planthopper in Rice?
answer: Brown Planthopper (பழுப்பு தத்துப்பூச்சி) is a sap-sucking insect affecting Rice. Damage symptoms: Hopper burn: yellowing and drying of plants in circular patches. Management: Avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties, encourage natural predators like spiders and mirid bugs.

question: How do I control Stem Borer in Rice?
answer: Stem Borer (தண்டு துளைப்பான்) is a larval boring insect affecting Rice, Maize, Sugarcane. Damage symptoms: Dead heart in vegetative stage, white ear head at reproductive stage. Management: Use pheromone traps, remove and destroy affected tillers, encourage egg-parasitoid release (Trichogramma).

question: How do I control Whitefly in Cotton?
answer: Whitefly (வெள்ளை ஈ) is a sap-sucking insect & virus vector affecting Cotton, Chilli, Tomato. Damage symptoms: Yellowing, sooty mould from honeydew, transmits leaf curl viruses. Management: Use yellow sticky traps, avoid excess nitrogen, encourage natural predators; rotate non-host crops.

question: How do I control Fall Armyworm in Maize?
answer: Fall Armyworm (இலை உண்ணும் புழு) is a leaf/whorl feeding caterpillar affecting Maize. Damage symptoms: Window-pane feeding damage on young leaves, ragged holes on whorl leaves. Management: Scout fields regularly, hand-pick egg masses, encourage natural enemies, use pheromone traps for monitoring.

question: How do I control Pod Borer in Groundnut?
answer: Pod Borer (காய் துளைப்பான்) is a larval boring insect affecting Groundnut, Blackgram, Pulses. Damage symptoms: Circular holes bored into pods/flowers, larval frass visible. Management: Deploy pheromone traps, encourage bird perches, avoid continuous monoculture.

question: How do I control Thrips in Chilli?
answer: Thrips (நுண்பூச்சி) is a rasping-sucking insect affecting Chilli, Onion, Groundnut. Damage symptoms: Silvery streaks on leaves, curling and crinkling of young leaves. Management: Use blue sticky traps, avoid moisture stress, encourage predatory mites and bugs.

question: Which crops grow well in Alluvial Soil?
answer: Alluvial Soil (வண்டல் மண்) is characterized by: Fertile, well-drained, rich in potash, deposited by rivers. It suits crops such as Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, Maize. Most fertile Indian soil type found in river plains and deltas; good for a wide crop range.

question: Which crops grow well in Black Cotton Soil (Regur)?
answer: Black Cotton Soil (Regur) (கருப்பு பருத்தி மண்) is characterized by: High clay content, high water-retention, cracks when dry. It suits crops such as Cotton, Groundnut, Sugarcane, Sorghum. Rich in lime, iron, magnesium; retains moisture well but drains slowly, needs careful water management.

question: Which crops grow well in Red Soil?
answer: Red Soil (செம்மண்) is characterized by: Low nitrogen and organic matter, well-drained, red due to iron oxide. It suits crops such as Groundnut, Millets, Pulses, Tobacco. Common in Tamil Nadu uplands; responds well to organic manure and balanced fertilization.

question: Which crops grow well in Laterite Soil?
answer: Laterite Soil (லேட்டரைட் மண்) is characterized by: Acidic, low fertility, high iron/aluminium content. It suits crops such as Cashew, Tea, Coffee, Rubber. Found in high rainfall regions; needs liming and organic matter to improve fertility.

question: Which crops grow well in Sandy Loam?
answer: Sandy Loam (மணல் கலந்த களிமண்) is characterized by: Good drainage, moderate water-holding capacity, easy to till. It suits crops such as Groundnut, Vegetables, Chilli. Warms quickly in spring and is easy to work, but may need more frequent irrigation.

question: Which crops grow well in Clayey Soil?
answer: Clayey Soil (களிமண்) is characterized by: High water-retention, poor drainage, nutrient-rich. It suits crops such as Rice, Sugarcane. Suitable for standing-water crops like rice; needs good drainage management for other crops.
